section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: For some time the SharedCLibrary core (library chunk ID 2) has provided two additional functions over those documented in the PRMs. The _clib_version function, used to read the C library details, has been expanded to give more detail on the components that make up the library. This document provides a description of these functions.

subsection.title: Calling conventions
subsection.p: All these functions use APCS-R or APCS-32 (dependent on linkage) calling conventions.

subsubsection.title: _clib_version (entry number 180)
subsubsection.p: This function returns a read-only string giving information on the C library. The string is composed of a number of newline delimited fields. Each field describes a component of the shared library, with the first field describing the overall features of the library.
The initial field will take the form:
where <qualifiers> is a sequence of strings prefixed by a '/' character to indicate the facilities offered by the core library. The only defined qualifier at present is /R:

value-table.value: Indicates that the format of the jmp_buf array is fixed to the logical APCS-A bindings of registers. That is, the format is: v4-v6, fp, sp, sl, lr, f4-f7

subsubsection.p: Subsequent fields within the returned string describe the component versions in the form:

item.p: The <version> is a 3 digit decimal number indicating the version number of that component.
The <date> is a standard RISC OS date string ("DD MMM YYYY") giving the date of this version of the component.

The <qualifiers> are formed in a similar manner to the overall features but the qualifiers should be interpreted on a component-specific basis. No qualifiers have been defined for any of the components.

subsubsection.p: The current component names which may be used to construct the C library are:

value-table.value: The Run Time System Kernel which manages the environment used by the C library
Core C library functions
Low-level C functions (primarily variable length arrays, and 64bit operations)
High-level C functions (all other C99-specific features)
Name allocated, but unused
Indicates that the C library is part of the 'SharedCLibrary' module.

subsubsection.p: The prior definition of this function placed no meaning on the string returned, and did not declare that the returned string was const. This definition improves that description. Under earlier versions of the Shared C Library (and ANSILib), this function would return a string in the form:

where <cppdate> is a date as produced by the C pre-processor __DATE__ macro (MMM DD YYY). The new format retains a similar style to this earlier form and so should be machine-parseable by code which previously interpreted the string value. The new format remains printable, so should be usable for diagnostic purposes.

subsubsection.title: _swi (entry number 183) and _swix (entry number 184)
subsubsection.p: These functions provide a generic method of calling RISC OS SWIs from C or C++.
Two functions are provided:

item.p: _swi for calling SWIs without setting the X bit
_swix which sets the X bit before calling the SWI.

subsubsection.p: swi_number is the number of the SWI to be called. This should never have the X bit set.
mask (the flags argument of _swi) is a word containing an input and output register mask, a return register, and a block parameter register.
The arrangement of the mask is as follows:

value-table.value: Set if R(N) is passed to the SWI.
Unused.
Set if a local block parameter is to be passed to the SWI
Register number for local block parameter if bit 11 set.
Register number to be returned from a _swi call. This is only applicable to _swi as _swix always returns either 0 or an error pointer.
Unused.
Set if the PC (including the flags) is to be output.
Set if R(31-N) is output from the SWI (ie bit 31 corresponds to R0, bit 22 corresponds to R9).

subsubsection.p: If a register is specified as a return register (bits 16-19) it must not also be specified as an output register in the output register mask (bits 22-31).
If a register is specified as a local block parameter register it must not also be specified as an input register in the input register mask (bits 0-9).
If the PC is specified as a return register (ie bits 16-19 = 15) or as an output register (bit 21 = 1) the value returned will contain the flags in bits 28 to 31 (28 = V, 29 = C, 30 = Z, 31 = N).
The remainder of the variadic arguments are as follows (in order):

item.p: The word value of each input register in order from 0 to 9 as specified by bits 0 to 9 of the mask.
The address of a word to be written for each output register in order from 0 to 9 as specified by bits 31 downto 22 of the mask.
The address of a word to be written with the PC value on exit from the SWI if bit 21 of the register mask is set.

subsubsection.p: If bit 11 is set the remainder of the arguments are placed in order in a parameter block and the address of the parameter block is passed to the SWI in the register specified by bits 12-15.
The macros are as follows:

value-table.value: Specifies that R(n) is used on input
Specifies that R(n) is output
Specifies that R(n) is a block parameter
Specifies that R(n) is returned from _swi.

subsubsection.p: The values of the macros should be ORed together to produce the value for the mask.
The following constants are defined:

value-table.value: The register containing the flags (currently 15)
Mask for the C bit in _FLAGS
Mask for the Z bit in _FLAGS
Mask for the N bit in _FLAGS
